## What you did
- Traced Orbitly's ~8% iOS funnel drop to your own #240 dedupe: kestrel-ios 3.2.0 switched `event_id` to a per-session counter, so distinct events were discarded as duplicates — ~1.18M legitimate Orbitly events (≈8.1% of their iOS volume), plus 3,812 for Zest's pilot store app [1].
- Rekeyed the dedupe on project:device:event_id (genuine replays still dropped), opened PR #247 with Maya as reviewer, and drafted the note asking the iOS team to restore UUIDs in 3.2.1 [1].

## What changed
- Maya says the logic looks right and will approve on green CI, but wants the dropped-event count for Thursday's call with Orbitly — you have it: ~1.18M, 8.1% of iOS volume [2][1].
- From the 12/11 incident review prep: you owe an alert on the ingest dead-letter queue above 1,000 messages, before Friday's review [7].
- Noa's final postmortem is up and credits your root-cause section; she presents it at Friday's incident review [3].
- Rachel closed Zest's Zendesk ticket, their dashboards confirmed complete [6].

## What is still open
- #247 must merge and deploy *before* the rebackfill: then replay prj_0rb1 (≈40 min) and prj_z3st from 13/11 out of landing, and check `ingest_dedupe_dropped_total{project="prj_0rb1"}` stays near zero — the reminder you asked for [1].
- The iOS-team note on `event_id` is still a draft; it needs sending [1].
